details: China's economy expanded by 4.5% year-on-year in the third quarter of 2026, surpassing analysts' expectations of 4.4% growth. This rebound, improving from the 4.3% in the previous quarter, eases pressure on policymakers for more aggressive stimulus measures to meet the annual target. The stronger growth was notably supported by robust exports and factory activity.
title: China's Q3 GDP Grows 4.5%, Beats Forecast

details: Oil prices declined in early Asian trading on Monday after the United States President Donald Trump waived sanctions and tariffs on Russia, a move that could lead to increased Russian fuel exports to global markets. Brent crude futures fell to $108.80 per barrel. This development introduces potential for increased supply, although ongoing disruptions in Middle Eastern crude flows continue to limit a sustained price drop.
title: Oil Prices Fall on US Waiver of Russian Sanctions
